source.title: Ulster Herald, 3 June 1933, p. 5 ("Council contest: result in Killeter division"); Irish News, 2 June 1933, p. 5 ("Tyrone results"); Derry Journal, 26 April 1933, p. 1
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: votes and majority as printed: 'O'KANE, 635; M'LOUGHLIN 293 ... The total poll was 932, and there were 5 spoiled votes' (Ulster Herald, 3 June 1933); the Irish News of 2 June prints the same votes and 'Majority for O'Kane, 342'.

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1933. Polling took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933: 'The voting in the Local Government Elections in Tyrone took place on Wednesday and passed without incident. There was one County Council contest, that in Killeter division of Castlederg Union' (Ulster Herald, 3 June 1933, p. 5). The Belfast News-Letter of 26 April 1933, p. 6 likewise reports the Clogher withdrawal and says 'There will thus be only one contest for County Council honours in the Nationalist division of Killeter.' Killeter: Denis O'Kane (Nat.) 635, Francis M'Laughlin (Nat.) 293, majority 342, total poll 932, 5 spoiled (Ulster Herald, 3 June 1933, p. 5; Irish News, 2 June 1933, p. 5). Clogher: Major William Stewart (U.) returned unopposed on the withdrawal of Mr. W. H. Smith (Belfast News-Letter, 26 April 1933, p. 6). The other 25 divisions are recorded from the Mid-Ulster Mail's full list of the nominations (22 April 1933, p. 6, page image read): 22 single nominations, returned unopposed, and Cookstown, Coagh and Strabane, where no nomination was lodged and the retiring members continued to sit. Labels are as printed. (The earlier reconstruction of these 25 from the 1939 list is replaced; five of its names differ from the 1933 list.) O'Kane defeated the retiring member M'Laughlin; both Nationalists. The Ulster Herald prints the total poll as 932 with 5 spoiled votes, but the votes sum to 928 valid + 5 = 933, so the poll and spoiled figures are left out. Both names are on the cited page, which prints M'Loughlin; the Irish News prints M'Laughlin.
